body:
@sepo-agent /implement

## Goal

Stop Sepo's live progress-comment updates from spawning a new Agent Entrypoint workflow run on every edit.

## Observed impact

A ten-minute observation in `co-evolving/hub` on 2026-08-13 found **48 secondary Agent Entrypoint runs** caused by two successful `/answer` progress comments:

- [Hub #428](https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/issues/428): 15 secondary runs — 14 cancelled and 1 skipped — while the primary [answer run 31674450364](https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/actions/runs/31674450364) was updating its progress comment.
- [Hub #432](https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/issues/432): 33 secondary runs — 31 cancelled and 2 skipped — while the primary [answer run 31674724279](https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/actions/runs/31674724279) was updating its progress comment.
- Representative recursive runs: [31674848359](https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/actions/runs/31674848359) and [31675339673](https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/actions/runs/31675339673). Their event actor and triggering actor are both `sepo-agent-app[bot]`, event `issue_comment`.

The answer runs completed, and the job-level bot guard prevented substantive routing, but it cannot prevent the workflow-run objects from being created. The churn pollutes Actions history and repeatedly enters cancellation/skip handling every approximately 10 seconds.

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml` subscribes to `issue_comment`, `pull_request_review_comment`, and `discussion_comment` with `types: [created, edited]`. The progress reporter repeatedly PATCHes one comment using the App credential. GitHub creates the workflow run before the entrypoint job's `github.event.sender.type != 'Bot'` condition can skip it.

## Compatibility constraint

Do not blindly remove edited-comment support. Issue #455 and open PR #456 deliberately model newly added explicit commands on human-edited comments. Preserve that behavior if practical, or make any decision to remove it explicit and reconcile #456.

A likely direction worth testing is to perform self-authored progress comment creation/updates/finalization with the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, whose events do not recursively start workflows, while retaining the App token for operations that require the Sepo App identity or permissions. Verify whether token identity and cross-author comment updates permit this before settling the design.

## Acceptance criteria

- A live progress run that updates its issue/PR comment repeatedly creates **zero secondary Agent Entrypoint runs** from those self-updates.
- Normal newly created human commands still route.
- Human edited-comment command behavior remains consistent with the settled #455/#456 policy, unless the PR explicitly revises and reconciles that policy.
- Progress rendering, final response replacement, and authorized cancellation continue to work.
- Token scopes remain least-privilege; no App/PAT credential is exposed to the agent process.
- Add focused tests for workflow/token wiring and the preserved trigger behavior, plus a regression note explaining why job-level bot filtering alone is insufficient.

Evidence originated in: https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/issues/428 and https://github.com/co-evolving/hub/issues/432
